name: push_up
description: A classic bodyweight pushing exercise that builds chest, shoulder, and tricep strength while engaging the core.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle from your body.
Press back up to the starting position, maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Keep your core braced throughout the movement.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike upward.
Flaring elbows out to 90 degrees, stressing the shoulder joint.
Not reaching full lockout at the top of the movement.

name: diamond_push_up
description: A push-up variation with hands close together forming a diamond shape, placing greater emphasis on the triceps.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with hands together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers touching to form a diamond shape.
Lower your chest toward your hands, keeping elbows close to your sides.
Press back up to full arm extension.
Keep your body in a rigid straight line throughout.
commonMistakes: Allowing the hips to sag or rise during the movement.
Letting elbows flare outward instead of tracking back along the torso.

name: pike_push_up
description: A push-up variation performed in a pike position that shifts load to the shoulders, mimicking an overhead press.
instructions: Start in a downward-dog position with hips raised high and body forming an inverted V.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor.
Press back up by extending your elbows, returning to the pike position.
Keep feet hip-width apart and core engaged throughout.
commonMistakes: Not maintaining a high enough hip position, reducing shoulder engagement.
Letting the elbows flare out excessively rather than tracking slightly back.

name: dips_on_chair
description: A tricep-focused dip performed with hands placed on the edge of a chair or bench, suitable for home workouts.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair and place your hands beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your hips off the chair with legs extended or bent at 90 degrees.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Press through your palms to return to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Allowing the shoulders to shrug up toward the ears at the bottom.
Bending the elbows outward instead of tracking them straight back.

name: incline_push_up
description: A beginner-friendly push-up variation performed with hands elevated on a surface, reducing the percentage of bodyweight lifted.
instructions: Place your hands on an elevated surface such as a bench, step, or countertop, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Walk your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the surface by bending your elbows.
Push back up to full arm extension.
commonMistakes: Sagging the hips, which removes core engagement.
Using a surface that is too low, making the movement too similar to a flat push-up before you are ready.

name: superman
description: A prone bodyweight exercise that strengthens the posterior chain, particularly the lower back and glutes.
instructions: Lie face down on a mat with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor as high as comfortable.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your glutes and back muscles.
Slowly lower back to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Holding the breath instead of breathing steadily.
Jerking the body up rather than lifting with controlled muscle contraction.

name: bodyweight_squat
description: A fundamental lower-body exercise that builds quad, glute, and hamstring strength with no equipment.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest tall and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward during the descent or ascent.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the squat.
Rising onto the toes instead of keeping heels grounded.

name: reverse_lunge
description: A unilateral lower-body exercise that targets the quads and glutes while improving balance and hip stability.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or at your sides.
Step one foot straight back and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front shin vertical and chest upright.
Push through your front heel to return to standing, then repeat on the other side.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee drift past the toes, increasing joint stress.
Leaning the torso forward instead of staying upright.

name: glute_bridge
description: A floor-based hip extension exercise that isolates the glutes and strengthens the posterior chain.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Hold at the top for one to two seconds, maintaining glute contraction.
Lower your hips back to the floor with control.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lower back instead of using the glutes to drive the movement.
Letting the knees collapse inward at the top of the bridge.

name: step_up
description: A unilateral lower-body exercise using a step or bench that builds quad and glute strength while improving balance.
instructions: Stand facing a step or bench that is roughly knee height.
Place one foot fully on the step and drive through that heel to lift your body up.
Bring the trailing foot up to stand on the step, then step back down with control.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
commonMistakes: Pushing off the back foot instead of driving purely through the front leg.
Letting the front knee cave inward as you step up.

name: calf_raise
description: An isolation exercise for the calf muscles performed by rising onto the toes from a standing position.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Slowly rise onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower your heels back to the floor with control.
For added range, perform on the edge of a step.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the movement without achieving full range of motion.
Rolling the ankles outward instead of rising straight up.

name: lateral_lunge
description: A side-to-side lunge that targets the inner thighs and glutes while improving hip mobility.
instructions: Stand with feet together and hands clasped in front of your chest.
Take a wide step to one side and sink your hips back and down over that foot, keeping the opposite leg straight.
Push through the bent leg's heel to return to the starting position.
Alternate sides each rep.
commonMistakes: Allowing the stepping knee to cave inward.
Leaning the torso too far forward instead of sitting the hips back.

name: plank
description: An isometric core exercise that builds stability and endurance throughout the entire trunk.
instructions: Place forearms on the floor with elbows directly under shoulders, hands flat or clasped.
Extend your legs behind you, resting on your toes.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag, placing stress on the lower back.
Piking the hips upward, reducing core activation.
Holding the breath instead of breathing throughout the hold.

name: dead_bug
description: A supine core stability exercise that trains anti-extension strength while improving coordination.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms pointing toward the ceiling and knees bent at 90 degrees above your hips.
Brace your core to press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and extend the opposite leg simultaneously.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch away from the floor as limbs extend.
Moving too quickly and losing spinal stability.

name: bicycle_crunch
description: A dynamic core exercise that targets the obliques and rectus abdominis through a rotational cycling motion.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and knees bent at 90 degrees off the floor.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating the opposite elbow toward it.
Simultaneously extend the other leg out straight.
Alternate sides in a controlled, smooth cycling motion.
commonMistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands instead of using the core to rotate.
Rushing the movement and losing rotational range.

name: mountain_climber
description: A dynamic full-body exercise combining core stability with cardio, performed from a high plank position.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with wrists under shoulders and body in a straight line.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs.
Keep your hips low and level throughout the movement.
Maintain a braced core and steady breathing.
commonMistakes: Allowing the hips to bounce up with each knee drive.
Placing the hands too far forward, which shifts weight away from the core.

name: hollow_hold
description: An advanced isometric core exercise that builds deep abdominal strength and body tension.
instructions: Lie on your back and press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Raise your legs to about 30-45 degrees and lift your shoulders off the floor.
Extend your arms overhead, keeping them close to your ears.
Hold this banana-shaped position, breathing steadily.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor, indicating the core is not braced enough.
Raising the legs too high, which reduces the difficulty and core challenge.

name: dumbbell_shoulder_press
description: A seated or standing overhead pressing movement that builds shoulder size and strength.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward.
Press the dumbbells directly overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the weights back to shoulder height with control.
Keep your core braced and avoid arching the lower back.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back excessively to compensate for tight shoulders.
Pressing the dumbbells at an angle rather than straight overhead.

name: dumbbell_row
description: A unilateral pulling exercise that develops upper back, lat, and bicep strength.
instructions: Place one hand and same-side knee on a bench for support, holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Let the dumbbell hang at arm's length with a neutral grip.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, driving the elbow straight back.
Lower the dumbbell under control and repeat for all reps before switching sides.
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso to generate momentum instead of pulling with the back.
Pulling the dumbbell toward the chest rather than the hip, reducing lat engagement.

name: dumbbell_curl
description: An isolation exercise for the biceps performed with dumbbells in a standing or seated position.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended and palms facing forward.
Keeping your elbows tucked at your sides, curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the weights slowly back to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to help lift the weight, taking tension off the biceps.
Letting the elbows drift forward during the curl.

name: dumbbell_lateral_raise
description: A shoulder isolation exercise that targets the medial deltoid by raising dumbbells out to the sides.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing inward.
With a slight bend in the elbows, raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top with a slight forward tilt of the dumbbells.
Lower the weights slowly back to your sides.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and swinging the body to initiate the lift.
Shrugging the shoulders up rather than lifting through the arms.

name: goblet_squat
description: A squat variation holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height that promotes an upright torso and deep squat mechanics.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell vertically by one end at chest height, elbows pointing down.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned slightly outward.
Squat down until your elbows touch the inside of your knees, keeping your chest tall.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
commonMistakes: Letting the torso lean forward excessively rather than staying upright.
Knees caving inward at the bottom of the squat.

name: dumbbell_rdl
description: A hip hinge movement with dumbbells that targets the hamstrings and glutes through a controlled lowering phase.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs with a neutral grip.
Hinge at your hips, pushing them back, and lower the dumbbells along your legs.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and a flat back throughout.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing, squeezing your glutes at the top.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as the dumbbells descend.
Bending the knees too much, turning the movement into a squat.

name: dumbbell_split_squat
description: A unilateral lunge-pattern exercise with dumbbells that develops single-leg strength and stability.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and step one foot forward and one foot back into a staggered stance.
Lower your back knee toward the floor while keeping your front shin vertical.
Keep your torso upright and core braced throughout.
Press through your front heel to return to the top position.
commonMistakes: Placing the feet too close together, causing balance issues.
Letting the front knee track inward rather than staying over the second toe.

name: arm_circles
description: A dynamic shoulder warm-up exercise that increases blood flow and mobility in the shoulder joint.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and extend both arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Make small forward circles gradually increasing to large circles.
After 15 seconds, reverse the direction.
Keep your posture tall and core lightly engaged.
commonMistakes: Tensing the shoulders and neck instead of staying relaxed.
Skipping the direction reversal, which limits full shoulder mobility.

name: leg_swings
description: A dynamic lower-body warm-up that mobilizes the hip joint through forward-back and lateral swinging motions.
instructions: Stand on one leg, holding a wall or sturdy surface for balance.
Swing the free leg forward and back in a controlled arc, gradually increasing range.
After 15 seconds, switch to lateral swings across the body.
Repeat on the other leg.
commonMistakes: Swinging too aggressively before the hip is warmed up.
Allowing the standing hip to shift rather than staying stable.

name: cat_cow
description: A gentle spinal mobility exercise performed on all fours that warms up the spine and core.
instructions: Begin on all fours with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale as you drop your belly toward the floor and lift your head and tailbone (cow).
Exhale as you round your spine toward the ceiling and tuck your chin and pelvis (cat).
Flow between positions slowly, coordinating movement with your breath.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the movement without using the breath to guide it.
Moving only through the lower back rather than mobilizing the entire spine.

name: childs_pose
description: A restorative yoga stretch that releases tension in the lower back, hips, and shoulders.
instructions: Kneel on a mat, sit your hips back toward your heels, and extend your arms forward on the floor.
Lower your chest and forehead toward the ground.
Breathe deeply and allow your hips and lower back to relax with each exhale.
Hold the position for the full duration.
commonMistakes: Holding the breath instead of using deep breathing to deepen the stretch.
Not sitting the hips far enough back, reducing the stretch in the lower back.

name: standing_quad_stretch
description: A standing stretch targeting the quadriceps, performed by pulling one foot toward the glutes.
instructions: Stand on one foot, using a wall for balance if needed.
Bend the other knee and grasp the ankle or foot behind you.
Pull your heel toward your glutes until you feel a stretch in the front of the thigh.
Hold for the full duration, then switch legs.
commonMistakes: Letting the knee of the stretching leg flare outward rather than pointing straight down.
Leaning forward at the hips instead of standing tall.

name: seated_hamstring_stretch
description: A floor-based stretch that targets the hamstrings, performed from a seated forward-fold position.
instructions: Sit on the floor with both legs extended straight in front of you.
Sit tall and hinge forward from your hips, reaching your hands toward your feet.
Hold the position when you feel a comfortable stretch in the back of your thighs.
Breathe deeply and try to lengthen your spine with each inhale.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back from the upper spine rather than hinging from the hips.
Forcing the stretch by pulling aggressively, which can cause the hamstrings to tighten as a protective response.
